url: /commit-jazzer/guide/getting-started.md

# Getting started

commit-jazzer asks a few questions (type, scope, title, …) and writes a [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org) message with an emoji. It needs Node.js 22.13 or newer and git.

## Install

::: code-group

```sh [npm]
npm install --save-dev commit-jazzer
```

```sh [pnpm]
pnpm add --save-dev commit-jazzer
```

```sh [yarn]
yarn add --dev commit-jazzer
```

```sh [bun]
bun add --dev commit-jazzer
```

:::

The package installs the command under two names, `jazzer` and `commit-jazzer`. Without installing, use the package name: `npx commit-jazzer`. (`npx jazzer` would download an unrelated package called `jazzer`.)

## Commit

Stage your changes and run:

```sh
npx jazzer
```

It asks the questions, shows the message, and runs `git commit` once you confirm. Options for `git commit` go after `--`:

```sh
npx jazzer -- --no-verify -S
```

A script makes it shorter for the team:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "commit": "jazzer"
  }
}
```

## Or let `git commit` ask

With the hook installed, a plain `git commit` asks the questions and opens the editor with the message filled in. `git commit -m "…"`, merges and amends are left alone, and so are commits from IDEs and GUI clients, which have no terminal to ask in.

```sh
npx jazzer init --hook          # install
npx jazzer init --remove-hook   # remove
```

`init --hook` also writes a config to the repository root when there is none. `git commit -m` still skips the questions; `npx jazzer init --lint` adds a `commit-msg` hook that checks those messages with `jazzer lint`.

The hook goes to `.husky/prepare-commit-msg` when the project uses [husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/), and to git's hooks directory otherwise (`core.hooksPath` is respected). See [Recipes](./recipes#git-hooks) for lefthook and simple-git-hooks.

## Or keep using `git cz`

If the team already runs [Commitizen](https://github.com/commitizen/cz-cli), point it at commit-jazzer:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "commitizen": {
      "path": "commit-jazzer"
    }
  }
}
```

For a global setup, install both packages globally and put the path into `~/.czrc`:

```sh
npm install --global commitizen commit-jazzer
echo '{ "path": "commit-jazzer" }' > ~/.czrc
```

## Configure

Everything works without a config. To change the questions, the types or the format, create one:

```sh
npx jazzer init        # jazzer.config.json
npx jazzer init --ts   # jazzer.config.ts
```

Continue with [Configuration](./configuration), or open the [Playground](/playground) to see how the options change the message.

## Uninstall

```sh
npx jazzer init --remove-hook   # if you installed the hook
npm uninstall commit-jazzer
```

Then delete `jazzer.config.*` and the `config.commitizen` entry of `package.json`, if you added them.

url: /commit-jazzer/guide/message-format.md

# Message format

## The default

```text
<type>(<scope>)!: <emoji> <title>

<description>

<comment>

BREAKING CHANGE: <breaking>
Closes <issue>
Closes <issue>
```

Empty parts disappear, together with the blank lines around them. With only a type and a title the message is a single line:

```text
fix: 🐛 handle an empty config file
```

| Part               | Question    | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`             | type        | Chosen from the list; brings its emoji.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `(scope)`          | component   | Wrapped in parentheses only when given.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `!`                | breaking    | Added when the breaking change answer is not empty.                                                                                                                                      |
| `title`            | title       | First letter lower-cased (unless it is an acronym such as `API`), trailing period removed. Turn off with `lowercaseTitle: false`.                                                        |
| `description`      | description | The body. `\|` starts a new line (`breaklineChar`); one space around it is dropped, more is kept as indentation. Wrapped at 100 columns (`bodyLineLength`).                              |
| `comment`          | comment     | Another body paragraph. Not asked by default.                                                                                                                                            |
| `BREAKING CHANGE:` | breaking    | The footer semantic-release looks for.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Closes #12`       | issues      | One line per issue, so GitHub closes each of them. `12 13` becomes `#12` and `#13`; keys like `JIRA-7` stay; a typed `closes` or `fixes:` is dropped. The word comes from `issuePrefix`. |

## Why the emoji goes after the colon

Tools parse the header with a pattern like `type(scope)!: subject`. With the emoji after the colon it becomes part of the subject, so:

* commitlint with `@commitlint/config-conventional` accepts the message;
* semantic-release and conventional-changelog read the type, the scope and the breaking change correctly.

An emoji in front of the type (`✨ feat: …`) breaks both. The test suite lints and parses generated messages for every combination of fields to keep this true.

commitlint's `subject-case` rule cannot judge a subject that starts with an emoji. commit-jazzer lower-cases the title itself instead.

## Header length

commitlint rejects headers over 100 characters by default. While you type the title, the counter shows how much of `headerMaxLength` is left after the type, scope and emoji. When the breaking change question is still ahead, one character is kept for the `!`.

The answers have limits of their own: the title 70 characters, the scope 30, the issues 100. Change them with `baseQuestionsOptions[].options.validations.length`. The scope, the title and the breaking change must fit on one line, and the scope cannot contain parentheses.

## Changing the template

`template` is a [Handlebars](https://handlebarsjs.com/guide/) template. Values are inserted as typed: `&`, `<` and quotes are not escaped.

| Variable                                                                     | Value                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`, `component`, `title`, `description`, `comment`, `breaking`, `issues` | The answers.                                                         |
| `emoji`, `code`                                                              | The emoji of the type and its shortcode, e.g. `✨` and `:sparkles:`. |
| `scope`                                                                      | `(component)`, or empty.                                             |
| `bang`                                                                       | `!` for a breaking change, or empty.                                 |
| `issuePrefix`                                                                | The `issuePrefix` option.                                            |
| `issueFooter`                                                                | One `<issuePrefix> <issue>` line per issue.                          |

Shortcodes instead of unicode emoji: the default template with `{{code}}` in place of `{{emoji}}`.

```json
{
  "template": "{{type}}{{scope}}{{bang}}: {{code}} {{title}}\n\n{{description}}\n\n{{comment}}\n\n{{#if breaking}}BREAKING CHANGE: {{breaking}}{{/if}}\n{{issueFooter}}"
}
```

Questions whose answer the template never writes are not asked: with the 1.x format below only the type and the title are. The 1.x format:

```json
{
  "template": "{{type}}: {{emoji}} - {{title}}"
}
```

The only rule for valid Conventional Commits: keep `{{type}}{{scope}}{{bang}}: ` at the start of the first line.

Body lines are wrapped at `bodyLineLength`; footer lines (`BREAKING CHANGE: …`, `Closes #12`, `Co-authored-by: …`) are never wrapped, and a wrapped line never starts with `#`. In hook mode git removes lines that start with `#` after you close the editor, so don't start a body line with an issue number.

# Configuration

Without a config commit-jazzer uses the defaults. A config only needs the options you want to change.

## Where it is read from

1. `--config <path>`, or the file in `$JAZZER_CONFIG`; a relative path is relative to the current directory.
2. A project config. The search starts in the current directory and goes up to the root of the git repository; the first match wins:
   * the `jazzer` field of `package.json`
   * `.jazzerrc` or `.jazzerrc.json` (JSON)
   * `.jazzer.config.{json,ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`
   * `jazzer.config.{json,ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`
3. Your own config, for every repository without one: `~/.config/commit-jazzer/config.{json,ts,…}` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/commit-jazzer/`), then `~/.jazzerrc` or `~/.jazzerrc.json`.

Command-line flags override the config for one run. A project config wins over the commitlint rules, which win over your own config; the defaults fill the rest.

TypeScript configs need nothing extra: they are loaded with [jiti](https://github.com/unjs/jiti), and `import { defineConfig } from 'commit-jazzer'` works even when the package is installed globally.

::: warning A config file is code
A `.ts` or `.js` config runs when commit-jazzer starts, like an ESLint or Prettier config. In a repository you do not trust, look at its `jazzer.config.*` before committing there, or point `--config` at a JSON file of your own. The search never leaves the repository, so files in parent directories such as `/tmp` are not loaded.
:::

## JSON

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/commit-jazzer/schema.json",
  "scopes": ["api", "web", "docs"]
}
```

The `$schema` line gives autocompletion and inline errors in VS Code, WebStorm and other editors. Use `https://zilero232.github.io/commit-jazzer/commit-jazzer-schema.json` when the package is not installed locally.

## TypeScript

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'commit-jazzer';

export default defineConfig({
  scopes: ['api', 'web', 'docs'],
  addCustomCommitTypes: {
    release: { emoji: '🔖', code: ':bookmark:', description: 'Releasing a version' }
  }
});
```

## Validation

The config is checked before the first question. Unknown keys are errors too, so a typo does not pass silently:

```text
[commit-jazzer] Invalid jazzer.config.json:
✖ Unrecognized key: "languge"
```

## Taken from commitlint

When the project has a [commitlint](https://commitlint.js.org) config and `@commitlint/load` or `@commitlint/cli` installed, these rules fill the options your config does not set:

| commitlint rule        | Option                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type-enum`            | `availableCommitTypes`: the built-in types it lists                     |
| `scope-enum`           | `scopes`; as an error (level 2) it also sets `allowCustomScopes: false` |
| `header-max-length`    | `headerMaxLength`                                                       |
| `body-max-line-length` | `bodyLineLength`                                                        |

Turn it off with `"useCommitlint": false`.

## Suggested from the branch

On a branch such as `feat/PROJ-12-login` or `fix/42-crash`, the type and the issue are preselected; press Enter to accept or change them. The prefix can be a type name or a common variant (`feature`, `bugfix`, `hotfix`, `doc`, `tests`, …); an issue key counts when it is written in capitals. Only in a terminal: scripts and CI get exactly what their flags say. Turn it off with `"inferFromBranch": false`.

## Common changes

### Fewer questions

```json
{ "availablePromptQuestions": ["type", "title"] }
```

The questions are always asked in this order: `type`, `component`, `title`, `description`, `breaking`, `issues`, `comment`.

### A list of scopes

```json
{ "scopes": ["api", "web", "docs"], "allowCustomScopes": false }
```

The scope question becomes a search over the list. With `allowCustomScopes: false` only listed scopes are accepted, from the prompt and from `--scope`.

### Fewer types, changed types, new types

```json
{
  "availableCommitTypes": ["feat", "fix", "docs", "refactor", "test", "chore"],
  "baseCommitTypes": {
    "feat": { "emoji": "🎸" }
  },
  "addCustomCommitTypes": {
    "release": { "emoji": "🔖", "code": ":bookmark:", "description": "Releasing a version" }
  }
}
```

Custom types are always offered, after the built-in ones. Their names use letters, digits and `_`: Conventional Commits parsers read no `-` in a type. The full list is in [Commit types](/reference/commit-types).

### Frequent commits

```json
{
  "aliases": {
    "deps": { "type": "upgrade", "component": "deps", "title": "update dependencies" }
  }
}
```

`jazzer :deps` commits it without questions. Flags still apply: `jazzer :deps -i 31`. Alias types and scopes are checked when the config is loaded.

### Question text and limits

```json
{
  "baseQuestionsOptions": [
    {
      "key": "title",
      "message": "What does this commit do?",
      "options": { "validations": { "length": { "minMessageLength": 10, "maxMessageLength": 60 } } }
    },
    { "key": "issues", "options": { "required": true } }
  ]
}
```

### Language

```json
{ "language": "de" }
```

Supported: `en`, `ru`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `it`, `pt`, `pl`, `tr`, `uk`, `zh`, `ja`, `ko`.

### Profanity filter

On by default: an answer with a blocked word is rejected while you type. To mask words instead:

```json
{
  "badWordsOptions": {
    "checkHasProfaneWords": false,
    "replaceProfaneWords": true,
    "options": { "additionalBlockWords": ["foo"], "excludedWords": ["hell"], "placeholder": "#" }
  }
}
```

Turn it off with `"validateCommitBadWords": false`.

### Banner and confirmation

```json
{ "showBanner": true, "confirmCommit": false }
```

The banner is off by default and never shown without a terminal. `--banner`, `--no-banner` and `--yes` change these for one run.

Every option with its type and default is listed in [Config options](/reference/config).

# Recipes

## Git hooks

`jazzer init --hook` writes the hook for you. It runs the project's copy, then a global one, and lets the commit go on when neither is installed.

git gives hooks no terminal on stdin, so the prompts open `/dev/tty`. Where there is none (IDE git panels, GUI clients, Windows) the hook does nothing and git opens its editor as usual.

With another hook manager, run the project's copy the same way:

::: code-group

```sh [husky]
# .husky/prepare-commit-msg
[ -x node_modules/.bin/commit-jazzer ] && exec node_modules/.bin/commit-jazzer hook "$1" "$2"
exit 0
```

```yaml [lefthook]
# lefthook.yml
prepare-commit-msg:
  commands:
    jazzer:
      run: node_modules/.bin/commit-jazzer hook {1} {2}
      interactive: true
```

```json [simple-git-hooks]
{
  "simple-git-hooks": {
    "prepare-commit-msg": "node_modules/.bin/commit-jazzer hook \"$1\" \"$2\""
  }
}
```

:::

## Check messages written without the questions

`git commit -m` skips the questions, so its message can be anything. `jazzer init --lint` adds a `commit-msg` hook that runs `jazzer lint` on every message: the header format, the type, a closed scope list, a non-empty subject and the length limits from your config. Merges, reverts and `fixup!` commits pass as they are. `init --lint` refuses when your template does not start with `{{type}}`, as those messages would never pass.

```text
$ git commit -m "added stuff"
[commit-jazzer] The first line must look like "type(scope): subject", got "added stuff"
```

## Check commits with commitlint

commit-jazzer writes messages that pass `@commitlint/config-conventional`, and reads `scope-enum` and the length limits from your commitlint config (see [Configuration](./configuration#taken-from-commitlint)). Its built-in types go beyond the conventional list, so allow them:

```js
// commitlint.config.mjs (.mjs: `require('commit-jazzer')` only gives the Commitizen adapter)
import { BUILT_IN_COMMIT_TYPE_NAMES } from 'commit-jazzer';

export default {
  extends: ['@commitlint/config-conventional'],
  rules: {
    'type-enum': [2, 'always', BUILT_IN_COMMIT_TYPE_NAMES],
    // The subject starts with an emoji; commit-jazzer lower-cases the title itself.
    'subject-case': [0]
  }
};
```

## Releases with semantic-release

Use the `conventionalcommits` preset. `!` and `BREAKING CHANGE:` give a major release, `feat` a minor and `fix` a patch. Other types release nothing unless you add rules. Put `{ breaking: true, release: 'major' }` first: custom rules replace the defaults, so without it `refactor!:` would only be a patch.

```js
// release.config.js
export default {
  plugins: [
    [
      '@semantic-release/commit-analyzer',
      {
        preset: 'conventionalcommits',
        releaseRules: [
          { breaking: true, release: 'major' },
          { type: 'refactor', release: 'patch' },
          { type: 'security', release: 'patch' },
          { type: 'upgrade', release: 'patch' }
        ]
      }
    ],
    ['@semantic-release/release-notes-generator', { preset: 'conventionalcommits' }],
    '@semantic-release/npm',
    '@semantic-release/github'
  ]
};
```

## Monorepo scopes

Put the config in the repository root; it is found from every package directory. List the packages as scopes, resolved from the config file rather than the current directory:

```ts
// jazzer.config.ts
import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { defineConfig } from 'commit-jazzer';

export default defineConfig({
  scopes: readdirSync(new URL('./packages', import.meta.url), { withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory())
    .map((entry) => entry.name),
  allowCustomScopes: false
});
```

## Scripts, CI and coding agents

Without a terminal nothing is asked. Give the required answers (type and title by default) as flags; optional questions without a flag stay empty:

```sh
jazzer -t fix -s parser -m "handle empty input" -b "Empty files no longer crash the parser." -i 31
```

A missing required answer is an error that names the flag (`Missing answer for --title`). Nothing is guessed from the branch name either. In a terminal, `--yes` skips the confirmation and asks only the required questions without a flag. `--dry-run` prints the message instead of committing; `--retry` commits the last message again after a failed hook.

## Issue keys in the footer

commit-jazzer writes issue keys in the footer. Make the question mandatory and change the word:

```json
{ "issuePrefix": "Refs", "baseQuestionsOptions": [{ "key": "issues", "options": { "required": true } }] }
```

```text
feat(api): ✨ add rate limits

Refs JIRA-118
```

On a branch like `feat/JIRA-118-rate-limits` the key is suggested automatically.

url: /commit-jazzer/guide/migration.md
---
# Migrating from 1.x

2.0 is a rewrite. These are the changes to check.

## Requirements

* **Node.js 22.13 or newer.** 1.x claimed Node 14 support.
* The package is ESM. `require('commit-jazzer')` still works for Commitizen: it returns `{ prompter }`.

## Message format

The default template changed from

```text
{{type}}: {{emoji}} - {{title}}
```

to a full Conventional Commits message:

```text
{{type}}{{scope}}{{bang}}: {{emoji}} {{title}}

{{description}}
…
```

To keep the old format, set `"template": "{{type}}: {{emoji}} - {{title}}"`; then only the type and the title are asked, as the template writes nothing else.

Other changes in the output:

* The title is lower-cased and loses a trailing period. Set `lowercaseTitle: false` to keep it as typed.
* Values are no longer HTML-escaped: `a & b` stays `a & b` (1.x wrote `a &amp; b`).
* Each related issue gets its own footer line (`Closes #1`, `Closes #2`), so GitHub closes all of them.

## Questions

* The default questions are now `type`, `component`, `title`, `description`, `breaking` and `issues` (1.x: `type`, `title`). Set `availablePromptQuestions` to change them.
* `language` now selects the prompt language; 1.x always asked in Russian.
* An answer with a blocked word is rejected while you type, instead of the commit being aborted after the last question.
* A confirmation step shows the message before committing. Turn it off with `confirmCommit: false` or `--yes`.

## Banner

The banner is off by default, and its default footer (the "give us a star" lines) is gone. Set `"showBanner": true` to get it back; `showBannerOptions.options.footerMessages` adds footer lines.

## Config

* Unknown keys are errors. Fix the reported key or remove it.
* The search for a project config stops at the repository root instead of your home directory. A config in `~` now goes to `~/.config/commit-jazzer/config.json`, `~/.jazzerrc` or `~/.jazzerrc.json`.
* `showBannerOptions` colors are [`util.styleText`](https://nodejs.org/api/util.html#utilstyletextformat-text-options) styles. They have the same names as the chalk colors 1.x used (`blue`, `bgGray`, …); figlet fonts must exist (`Standard`, `Slant`, …).
* New config locations: `package.json` (`jazzer` field), `.jazzerrc`, and `.mts`/`.cts`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` configs.

## Types

* `CommitJazzerPrompterOptions` is now `JazzerConfig` (the old name is still exported, deprecated). Import types from `commit-jazzer`, not from `commit-jazzer/build/types`.
* Use `defineConfig` instead of annotating the object.

## Commit types

Added `chore`. Removed `fix-ci`: Conventional Commits parsers (and semantic-release) cannot read a `-` in a type; write `fix(ci)` instead, and rename custom types with a `-`. New emoji for types whose emoji or shortcode were wrong or duplicated: `review` 👌, `monitor` 🔊, `animation` 💫, `mock` 🤡, `experiment` ⚗️, `legal` 📄. Override them with `baseCommitTypes` if you prefer the old ones.

---
# FAQ

## The hook does not ask anything

* The hook skips commits that already have a message: `git commit -m`, `-F`, merges, squashes and `--amend`.
* It also skips commits without a terminal: IDE git panels, GUI clients, and Windows, where Node cannot open the terminal of a hook. git then opens its editor as usual.
* A hook in `.git/hooks` must be executable: `chmod +x .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg`.
* `core.hooksPath` set by another tool? `jazzer init --hook` writes the hook there; with husky it goes to `.husky/`.
* With `commit.template` set, git reports every commit as a template commit, and the hook leaves those alone.

## `npx jazzer` runs something else

`jazzer` is the command name, not the package name. Before installing, run `npx commit-jazzer`; after `npm install --save-dev commit-jazzer`, `npx jazzer` works too.

## Commitizen uses an old Inquirer. Does that matter?

No. Commitizen passes its Inquirer 8 to the adapter; commit-jazzer ignores it and uses the current `@inquirer` prompts.

## How do I commit with a message I already have?

`git commit -m "…"` as usual. With the hook installed it is left alone.

## A hook rejected my commit. Do I have to answer everything again?

No: `jazzer --retry` commits the last message again. The message of a `jazzer` commit that failed stays in `.git/commit-jazzer/last-message` until a commit goes through. Messages of the hook and of `git cz` are not stored there, but git keeps them in `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`.

## Can I use it without a terminal?

Yes. Pass the required answers as flags; see [Scripts, CI and coding agents](./recipes#scripts-ci-and-coding-agents).

## How does it compare to other tools?

As of October 2026, from the documentation of each tool:

|                                 | commit-jazzer                   | [cz-git / czg](https://cz-git.qbb.sh) | [gitmoji-cli](https://github.com/carloscuesta/gitmoji-cli) | [better-commits](https://github.com/Everduin94/better-commits) |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standalone CLI                  | ✅                              | ✅                                    | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                             |
| Commitizen adapter              | ✅                              | ✅                                    | —                                                          | —                                                              |
| `prepare-commit-msg` hook       | ✅                              | ✅                                    | ✅                                                         | —                                                              |
| Conventional Commits output     | ✅                              | ✅                                    | — (`:emoji: (scope): title`)                               | ✅                                                             |
| Non-interactive flags           | ✅                              | aliases                               | prefill only                                               | ✅                                                             |
| Reads the commitlint config     | scopes, lengths                 | ✅                                    | —                                                          | —                                                              |
| Type and ticket from the branch | ✅                              | via recipe                            | —                                                          | ✅                                                             |
| Config                          | JSON / TS / JS / `package.json` | JS / TS / commitlint config           | JSON / `package.json`                                      | JSONC                                                          |
| Built-in prompt translations    | 13 languages                    | — (texts are configurable)            | —                                                          | —                                                              |
| AI suggestions                  | —                               | ✅                                    | —                                                          | —                                                              |

Pick cz-git if you want AI messages or one config file shared with commitlint; gitmoji-cli if you want gitmoji's own format.

## How do I add a language?

Copy `src/core/i18n/locales/en.json`, translate the values, and add the language to `LANGUAGES` in `src/shared/constants.ts` and to `src/core/i18n/i18n.ts`. A test checks that every language has the same keys and placeholders.

# Config options

Generated from the [JSON Schema](/commit-jazzer-schema.json), which is generated from the validation code, so this page always matches what the config loader accepts. Every option is optional.

---

---
url: /commit-jazzer/reference/cli.md
---
# CLI

The package installs one command under two names: `jazzer` and `commit-jazzer`.

## `jazzer [options] [-- <git commit arguments>]`

Asks the questions, shows the message and runs `git commit`. Exits with git's exit code.

### Answers

Each flag answers its question, which is then not asked. An empty value (`--breaking ""`) answers with nothing. A flag for a question that is not in `availablePromptQuestions` still goes into the message.

| Option                | Answers                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Commit type, e.g. `feat`.                |
| `-s, --scope <scope>` | Scope (the component).                   |
| `-m, --title <title>` | Title.                                   |
| `-b, --body <text>`   | Description; `\|` starts a new line.     |
| `--breaking <text>`   | Breaking change; adds `!` to the header. |
| `-i, --issues <ids>`  | Related issues, e.g. `"12, 34"`.         |
| `--comment <text>`    | Extra body paragraph.                    |

Flags are validated like typed answers: an unknown type, a scope outside `scopes` with `allowCustomScopes: false`, a title over the limit, a line break in a header field or parentheses in the scope is an error. So is an answer the template never writes (`--breaking` with a template without `{{breaking}}`), and `--retry` with answers.

### Options

| Option                    | Description                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-y, --yes`               | No confirmation; only required questions without a flag are asked.               |
| `-n, --dry-run`           | Print the message to stdout instead of committing. Does not need staged changes. |
| `-r, --retry`             | Commit the last message again, without questions.                                |
| `-c, --config <path>`     | Use this config file instead of searching. Also `$JAZZER_CONFIG`.                |
| `--banner`, `--no-banner` | Show or hide the banner for this run.                                            |
| `-a, --all`               | `git commit --all`.                                                              |
| `--amend`                 | `git commit --amend`.                                                            |
| `--no-verify`             | `git commit --no-verify`.                                                        |
| `-h, --help`              | Show the help.                                                                   |
| `-v, --version`           | Show the version.                                                                |

Everything after `--` goes to `git commit` unchanged, files included:

```sh
jazzer -- -S --author "Jane <jane@example.com>"
jazzer -- src/parser.ts
```

Without a terminal (CI, scripts, pipes) nothing is asked and nothing is guessed from the branch: optional answers without a flag stay empty, and a missing required one is an error naming its flag.

## `jazzer :<alias>`

Commits the answers of an [alias](/guide/configuration#frequent-commits) from the config, without questions or confirmation. Answer flags override the alias: `jazzer :deps -i 31`. `--alias <name>` is the same.

## `jazzer init`

Creates `jazzer.config.json` in the root of the repository (the current directory outside one). With a config present it exits with 1, unless `--force` replaces `jazzer.config.json`/`.ts`; with `--hook` or `--lint` it keeps the config and only installs the hooks. A config in `.jazzerrc` or `package.json` is never replaced.

| Option          | Description                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ts`          | Write `jazzer.config.ts` instead.                                                                                           |
| `--hook`        | Also install the `prepare-commit-msg` hook that asks the questions on `git commit`.                                         |
| `--lint`        | Also install the `commit-msg` hook that runs `jazzer lint` on every message.                                                |
| `--remove-hook` | Remove the hooks `init` installed; hooks written by someone else stay.                                                      |
| `-f, --force`   | Replace `jazzer.config.json` or `jazzer.config.ts` (leaving one of them). Other configs and other hooks are never replaced. |

Hooks go to `.husky/` when husky runs the hooks, and to git's hooks directory otherwise (`core.hooksPath` and worktrees are respected). They run the project's `commit-jazzer`, then a global one, and do nothing when neither is installed.

## `jazzer lint [file]`

Checks a commit message against the config: the `type(scope): subject` header, the type, a closed scope list, a non-empty subject, `headerMaxLength`, the blank line after the header and `bodyLineLength` for body lines. Reads `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` without a file. git's comment lines (`core.commentChar`) and the diff of `git commit -v` are ignored; merges, reverts, reapplies and `fixup!` commits pass. Exits with 1 when something is wrong.

| Option                | Description           |
| --------------------- | --------------------- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Use this config file. |

## `jazzer hook <file> [source]`

Fills the message file from a `prepare-commit-msg` hook; `file` and `source` are the hook's `$1` and `$2`. Commits that already have a message (`message`, `template`, `merge`, `squash`, `commit` sources) and commits without a terminal are left alone.

| Option                | Description           |
| --------------------- | --------------------- |
| `-c, --config <path>` | Use this config file. |

## Exit codes

| Code  | Meaning                                                                                                                  |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`   | Committed, printed with `--dry-run`, `init` or `lint` succeeded, or `hook` left a commit alone.                          |
| `1`   | Invalid arguments, config or answers; blocked words; nothing staged; a cancelled confirmation; a message `lint` rejects. |
| other | A failed `git commit`: its own exit code.                                                                                |
| `130` | Interrupted with Ctrl+C.                                                                                                 |

---

---
url: /commit-jazzer/reference/commit-types.md
---
# Commit types

The built-in types, in the order of the selection list. Limit them with `availableCommitTypes`, change one with `baseCommitTypes`, add your own with `addCustomCommitTypes` (see [Configuration](/guide/configuration#fewer-types-changed-types-new-types)).

---

---
url: /commit-jazzer/reference/api.md
---
# JavaScript API

The package is a CLI first. From JavaScript it offers what configs and Commitizen need; types are included.

## `defineConfig(config)`

Returns the config unchanged and types it, for autocompletion in `jazzer.config.ts` or `.js`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'commit-jazzer';

export default defineConfig({
  scopes: ['api', 'web']
});
```

## `JazzerConfig`

The type of a config, for configs that build the object elsewhere:

```ts
import type { JazzerConfig } from 'commit-jazzer';

const shared: JazzerConfig = { language: 'de' };
```

`CommitJazzerPrompterOptions`, the name from 1.x, still works and is deprecated.

## `BUILT_IN_COMMIT_TYPE_NAMES`

The names of the built-in commit types, e.g. for commitlint's `type-enum` (see [Recipes](/guide/recipes#check-commits-with-commitlint)).

## `prompter`

The Commitizen adapter. Commitizen finds it by itself through `"path": "commit-jazzer"`; you don't call it. `require('commit-jazzer')` returns only this function.

Anything else (running the questions, formatting or linting a message) goes through the CLI: `jazzer --dry-run` prints a message, `jazzer lint` checks one.
